title: Glycemic Impact of LINGO CGM in Primary Care
official: Assessing the Impact of an Over-the-Counter Continuous Glucose Monitor in Primary Care to Improve Metabolic Health for Adults of South Asian or Filipino Ancestry in California: LINGO Study
summary:
The aim of this study is to examine the impact of over-the-counter glucose monitoring (Lingo biosensor) to adults with non-insulin treated T2D or prediabetes in a Northern California primary care practice focusing on those of South Asian and Filipino ancestries. Comparisons will be made of (a) the use of the continuous glucose monitor alone or (b) use of the continuous glucose monitor together with culturally congruent, digital-delivered lifestyle education with (c) usual care (including patient handouts and in-clinic medical counseling).

This is a single-center, 3-arm randomized controlled trial (RCT) involving 225 Palo Alto Medical Foundation patients who are of self-proclaimed South Asian or Filipino ancestry. This is a pilot study for OTC CGMs. The study will include three arms, each enrolling 75 participants with an established diagnosis of non-insulin-treated type 2 diabetes or prediabetes, defined as an HbA1c of 6.0-6.4%, to examine changes in glycemic profiles measured by continuous glucose monitoring.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Palo Alto Medical Foundation patient who identifies as South Asian or Filipino
* ≥ 18 years of age at enrollment.
* Has an established diagnosis of type 2 diabetes or prediabetes, defined as an HbA1c of 6.0-6.4%
* Willing to wear a CGM device.

Exclusion Criteria:

Pregnancy

* Taking insulin
* Chronic kidney disease and on dialysis
* Any active clinically significant disease or disorder which, in the investigator's opinion, could interfere with participation in the study
